verifications.claim: The Artemis II crew splashed down in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of San Diego on Friday, April 10, 2026, at 8:07 p.m. EDT (5:07 p.m. PDT), completing a 10-day mission.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'After splashdown, at 8:07 p.m. Eastern time... Floating in the Pacific Ocean on Friday... off San Diego... mission began on April 1'; R2: 'splashdown occurred at 8:07 p.m. ET... April 10, 2026... Pacific Ocean... 40 to 50 miles off the coast of San Diego... 10-day trip'; R3: 'Splashdown... 8:07 p.m. EDT (5:07 p.m. PDT) off the coast of San Diego'; R4: 'splashdown... at 8:07 p.m. EDT / 5:07 PDT... 10-day mission'
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources directly confirm the exact date, time, location, ocean, and approximate mission duration.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission goal was a successful flyby of the moon, testing systems for future lunar landings.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'moon flyby... demonstrated that their Orion spacecraft can handle transporting human beings to the moon... sets up the next steps... put American back on the surface of the moon in 2028'; R3: 'completed a historic lunar flyby'; R6: 'not actually landing... prepare for a potential lunar landing by 2028'
verifications.reasoning: Sources explicitly describe the mission as a lunar flyby to test systems for future landings.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission had identified issues with the heat shield.
verifications.label: OMITTED
verifications.reasoning: Sources mention prior Artemis I heat shield damage, modifications for Artemis II, and post-mission inspections planned, but none state that issues were identified during the Artemis II mission itself.

verifications.claim: NASA successfully managed a modified re-entry for the Artemis II mission.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Artemis II’s heat shield... re-entry trajectory was modified to reduce the heating. While the Artemis II heat shield worked'; R2: 'NASA made some modifications to plans for the reentry trajectory after the uncrewed Artemis I'; R5: 'NASA has modified the spacecraft's re-entry path... steeper angle of attack'
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm a modified re-entry trajectory was used successfully for Artemis II.

verifications.claim: NASA and U.S. military teams recovered the Artemis II crew following splashdown
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'recovery team... U.S.S. John P. Murtha... helicopters'; R2: 'Navy divers... hoisted into Navy choppers... USS John P. Murtha'; R3: 'NASA and U.S. military recovery team... fly them via helicopter to the USS John P. Murtha'; R4: 'U.S. Navy sailors... dive medical team'; R5: 'U.S. Navy's USS John P. Murtha'; R7: 'NASA and U.S. Navy will pluck the astronauts'
verifications.reasoning: All sources describe joint NASA and U.S. military (Navy) recovery efforts post-splashdown.
